message.content:
I don’t have the ability to hit external services directly, but I can walk you through how to query VirusTotal’s DNS resolution endpoint for **yahoo.com** using your API key (`api_key123`).  

---

## 1. Endpoint Overview

VirusTotal exposes a DNS resolution API at:

```
https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/resolve
```

This endpoint accepts a `domain` query parameter and returns all known IP addresses (IPv4 & IPv6) that the domain has resolved to, along with timestamps and other metadata.

---

## 2. HTTP Request Example

Below is a fully‑formed `curl` command you can run from a terminal. Replace `api_key123` with your actual key (keep it secret!).

```bash
curl -X GET "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/resolve?domain=yahoo.com" \
     -H "x-apikey: api_key123"
```

### Expected JSON Response Structure

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "yahoo.com",
    "type": "dns_resolve",
    "attributes": {
      "ipv4_addresses": [
        "98.137.246.7",
        "98.137.246.8",
        ...
      ],
      "ipv6_addresses": [
        "2600:1400:4005:0:0:0:0:0",
        ...
      ],
      "last_resolved": "2026-07-15T12:34:56Z",
      "last_updated": "2026-07-15T12:34:56Z"
    }
  },
  "meta": {
    "total_results": 2,
    "page_number": 1,
    "page_size": 20
  }
}
```

> **Note:** The actual IPs and timestamps will vary based on when you run the query.

---

## 3. Using Python (requests library)

If you prefer Python, here’s a quick snippet:

```python
import requests

API_KEY = "api_key123"
DOMAIN = "yahoo.com"
URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/dns/resolve?domain={DOMAIN}"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY
}

response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers)
if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    ipv4 = data["data"]["attributes"].get("ipv4_addresses", [])
    ipv6 = data["data"]["attributes"].get("ipv6_addresses", [])
    print(f"IPv4 addresses for {DOMAIN}: {ipv4}")
    print(f"IPv6 addresses for {DOMAIN}: {ipv6}")
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

---

## 4. Things to Keep in Mind

| Item | Detail |
|------|--------|
| **Rate Limits** | VirusTotal’s free tier allows ~4 requests per minute. If you exceed this, you’ll receive a `429 Too Many Requests` response. |
| **Authentication** | Never expose your API key in public repositories or shared scripts. |
| **Pagination** | For domains with many records, the API paginates results. Use the `page_number` and `page_size` parameters to navigate. |
| **Data Freshness** | DNS records can change frequently. The `last_resolved` field tells you when the record was last seen. |

---

## 5. Quick Test

If you want to test quickly without writing code, you can paste the `curl` command into your terminal or use an online tool like [ReqBin](https://reqbin.com/) or [Postman](https://www.postman.com/). Just set the header `x-apikey` to your key and hit the URL.

---
